counterparts_needing_dossiers.name: Volga German Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic
Komuch (Committee of Members of the Constituent Assembly)

problems: Ukrainian SSR (8 pages) and RSFSR (18 pages) exceed the 5-page budget; the Civil War and 1939-1945 events mirror the pages cited in the Russian State, South Russia, Far Eastern Republic and Poland-front dossiers.

Cliopatria overlap: every Soviet-republic dossier here is an internal unit whose land lies inside Cliopatria Russian Republic (1917-1919), Republics of the Soviet Union (1920-1921) and Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (1922-1991) shapes; the renderer must not draw both as owners. Autonomous republics are modelled as vassal events (RSFSR, Ukrainian SSR, Uzbek SSR); the Transcaucasian federation is modelled as a loss and gain of each SSR country (March 1922, December 1936).

Page-date conflicts, kept in the notes: Treaty of Riga (February 1921 on the BSSR page, 18 March on the Riga page); Armenia joining the TSFSR (March vs 30 December 1922); Tajik SSR (15 October vs December 1929); Kirghiz renames (30 October, 15 December 1990, 5 February 1991); Karakalpakstan from the RSFSR or the Kazakh SSR; independence recognition 25 or 26 December 1991; RSFSR infobox area is a 1956 estimate marked citation needed.

The RSFSR dossier was revised late: the Karelian Isthmus now belongs to the Karelo-Finnish SSR from March 1940 and to the RSFSR from September 1944; the Estonian and Latvian strips are split into two gains. The Ukrainian SSR dossier gained the Moldavian ASSR vassal events.

Name collision: the Lithuanian SSR of 1918-1919 (merged into Litbel, a counterpart string in the Byelorussian SSR dossier) is a different state from the lithuanian-soviet-socialist-republic dossier (1940-1990).

Counterpart `ottoman-empire` stands for the Grand National Assembly government in 1921 (Cliopatria Republic of Turkey starts in 1924). The Far Eastern Republic dossier still warns on the counterpart state-of-buryat-mongolia (no dossier).

The gazetteer overcounts small coastal countries (Estonia 57,661, Latvia 79,411, Lithuania 74,858 km2 against 45,227, 64,589 and 65,200 km2 in the 1989 infoboxes) and undercounts Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and Kazakhstan; ratios are in the keyframe notes. Where the gazetteer lacks a name, circles are used (listed in gazetteer_names_needed).
Crimean ASSR and Volga German ASSR were not written (internal units; the RSFSR keyframe draws Crimea as core until 1954).
